analysis.investment_thesis: Identixweb is a tiny INR 9 Cr revenue Shopify-app shop with good ROE (24.8%) but no durable moat and no operating history to speak of. At INR 90 Cr market cap on ~INR 3 Cr profit, I'd rather wait a decade to see if the business is real.
key_strengths: High ROCE of 34.3% and ROE of 24.8% on a debt-free balance sheet
Revenue up 50% in FY25 (6→9 Cr) with operating income doubling to 6 Cr
Promoter holding firm at 62.99%, no borrowings
key_risks: Micro-scale (9 Cr revenue) totally dependent on Shopify ecosystem — no moat, platform risk
Equity ballooned from 10→31 Cr in FY25 (IPO dilution); FCF negative two years running
P/E 18.6 on a 3 Cr profit base means any stumble collapses the multiple
red_flags: Recent IPO with equity jumping 3x in one year — cash sitting on balance sheet inflates ROE optics
Negative free cash flow in FY24 (-4) and FY25 (-2) despite reported profits
Business is essentially a services shop reselling on someone else's platform (Shopify)
analysis.detailed_analysis:
This is exactly the kind of business I wouldn't touch. A five-year-old company doing INR 9 crore of revenue building apps on Shopify's platform has no circle of competence a long-term owner can rely on — Shopify changes its API or commercial terms and the whole thesis evaporates. The headline ROE of 24.8% and ROCE of 34.3% look attractive, but they're computed on a tiny capital base that just tripled via an IPO; the reserves line jumped from 3 to 21 Cr in FY25, so next year's ROE will mechanically compress as that cash sits idle. Meanwhile free cash flow has been negative in both FY24 and FY25 despite "profits" — a classic sign that reported earnings and actual owner cash don't line up.

At INR 90 Cr market cap on ~INR 3 Cr net profit, the trailing P/E of 18.6 is only reasonable if you believe the 50% revenue growth compounds for years. There's no evidence of pricing power, no switching costs (Shopify merchants churn apps constantly), no brand. Promoters at 63% is fine, but post-IPO insider behavior is unproven. I'd put this in the "too hard / too small / too new" pile and move on — there's no margin of safety and no moat worth paying for.
